ARABIC LANGUAGE — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #6
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: ARABIC LANGUAGE
TIME ALLOWED: 120 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. How would a girl say 'I am a pupil'? (1 mark)
   A. anaa tilmiidh
   B. haadhaa tilmiidh
   C. ismii tilmiidh
   D. anaa tilmiidha

2. What does the Arabic word السَّلَامُ عَلَيْكُمْ (as-salaamu ʿalaykum) mean? (1 mark)
   A. How are you? (to a boy)
   B. good morning (the reply)
   C. peace be upon you
   D. I

3. What does the Arabic sentence عِنْدِي أَخٌ وَأُخْتٌ mean? (1 mark)
   A. My father works.
   B. This is my mother.
   C. This is my father.
   D. I have a brother and a sister.

4. Which Arabic sentence means "The lamp is above the table." (1 mark)
   A. الْكِتَابُ عَلَى الطَّاوِلَةِ
   B. الْقِطَّةُ تَحْتَ السَّرِيرِ
   C. الْمِصْبَاحُ فَوْقَ الطَّاوِلَةِ
   D. الْقَلَمُ فِي الْحَقِيبَةِ

5. What does the Arabic sentence الْقِطَّةُ تَحْتَ السَّرِيرِ mean? (1 mark)
   A. The pen is in the bag.
   B. The book is on the table.
   C. The cat is under the bed.
   D. The lamp is above the table.

6. What does the Arabic word اِسْمَعْ (ismaʿ) mean? (1 mark)
   A. listen
   B. read
   C. write
   D. open the door

7. How is the Arabic word دَوْرِي read aloud in English letters? (1 mark)
   A. ʿiid
   B. ʿasiir
   C. mabruuk
   D. dawrii

8. What does hal do at the start of an Arabic question? (1 mark)
   A. It makes a yes or no question
   B. It means 'my'
   C. It means 'and'
   D. It means 'the'

9. Which word do you say to tell a friend it is now their turn? (1 mark)
   A. laa
   B. dawruka
   C. dawrii
   D. shukran

10. What does the Arabic word بُرْتُقَالٌ (burtuqaal) mean? (1 mark)
   A. fish
   B. eggs
   C. meat
   D. oranges

11. In the game Simon Says, how do learners show they are listening? (1 mark)
   A. They act only on the correct instruction
   B. They cover their ears
   C. They speak loudly
   D. They act on every instruction

12. Which word means 'with' in bi-yadii? (1 mark)
   A. ii
   B. fii
   C. yad
   D. bi

13. What does the Arabic word جِسْمٌ (jism) mean? (1 mark)
   A. leg
   B. body
   C. back
   D. neck

14. What does the Arabic word شَمْسٌ (shams) mean? (1 mark)
   A. weather
   B. sunny
   C. sun
   D. flower

15. Which is a good way to take care of the environment? (1 mark)
   A. Throw rubbish in the river
   B. Cut trees without planting new ones
   C. Plant trees and keep the surroundings clean
   D. Burn plastic in the open

16. What does tone mean in public speaking? (1 mark)
   A. The length of the speech
   B. The size of the audience
   C. How your voice sounds, for example friendly and clear
   D. The colour of your clothes

17. How do you read the syllable مَ? (1 mark)
   A. ma
   B. lu
   C. si
   D. bi

18. How do you read the syllable لَ? (1 mark)
   A. si
   B. la
   C. na
   D. su

19. What is the name of the Arabic letter ض? (1 mark)
   A. ghayn
   B. Daad
   C. thaa
   D. taa

20. What does the Arabic sentence مَرْحَبًا يَا أَحْمَدُ mean? (1 mark)
   A. My brother is small.
   B. My sister is beautiful.
   C. Hello, Ahmad.
   D. My grandfather is old (big in age).

21. How is the Arabic word جَدَّةٌ read aloud in English letters? (1 mark)
   A. ukht
   B. jadd
   C. jadda
   D. akh

22. Which is the correct blend of the syllables a + bun? (1 mark)
   A. buna
   B. bana
   C. abun
   D. nuba

23. How is the Arabic word أَنْفٌ read aloud in English letters? (1 mark)
   A. qalb
   B. anf
   C. fam
   D. ʿayn

24. How is the Arabic word بَطْنٌ read aloud in English letters? (1 mark)
   A. jism
   B. batn
   C. raʾs
   D. rijl

25. Which Arabic word means "river"? (1 mark)
   A. سَمَاءٌ
   B. مَطَرٌ
   C. شَمْسٌ
   D. نَهْرٌ

26. Which Arabic word means "window"? (1 mark)
   A. غُرْفَةٌ
   B. طَاوِلَةٌ
   C. مِصْبَاحٌ
   D. نَافِذَةٌ

27. How is the Arabic word مِلْعَقَةٌ read aloud in English letters? (1 mark)
   A. hadiiqa
   B. milʿaqa
   C. qalam
   D. baab

28. What is the short line ـ used for in Arabic letter tables? (1 mark)
   A. It shows where a letter joins to another
   B. It is a dot
   C. It is a full stop
   D. It is a vowel

29. Which letter completes the word _َمٌ to make fam (mouth)? (1 mark)
   A. ك (kaaf)
   B. ف (faa)
   C. ق (qaaf)
   D. م (miim)

30. In which direction is Arabic written? (1 mark)
   A. From right to left
   B. From left to right
   C. From the middle outwards
   D. From top to bottom only

31. Which Arabic word means "clock"? (1 mark)
   A. غُرْفَةٌ
   B. سَاعَةٌ
   C. مِصْبَاحٌ
   D. كُرْسِيٌّ

32. How is the Arabic word جَدِيدٌ read aloud in English letters? (1 mark)
   A. qalam
   B. jadiid
   C. mushmis
   D. fam

33. Which is the correct spelling of Thursday? (1 mark)
   A. الخميس
   B. الجميس
   C. الخمبس
   D. الحميس

34. Which word fills the gap in: ashrabu ____ (I drink the juice)? (1 mark)
   A. al-hafla
   B. al-ʿasiira
   C. baaluun
   D. al-kaʿka

35. What should you check on a food chart before posting it? (1 mark)
   A. The spelling, dots and marks
   B. Only the date
   C. Nothing
   D. Only the colour

36. What does shaping of characters mean? (1 mark)
   A. Using many colours
   B. Writing each letter in its correct shape
   C. Drawing pictures
   D. Writing very fast

37. Which Arabic word means "neck"? (1 mark)
   A. رَقَبَةٌ
   B. بَطْنٌ
   C. سِنٌّ
   D. جِسْمٌ

38. Which Arabic sentence means "The wind is strong." (1 mark)
   A. هَذَا مَطَرٌ
   B. الرِّيحُ قَوِيَّةٌ
   C. الشَّمْسُ حَارَّةٌ
   D. هَذِهِ شَمْسٌ

39. Which Arabic word means "flower"? (1 mark)
   A. سَحَابٌ
   B. غَائِمٌ
   C. زَهْرَةٌ
   D. مَطَرٌ

40. Which sentence is the best beginning of a paragraph about your house? (1 mark)
   A. al-kitaabu ʿalaa t-taawila
   B. haadhaa baytii
   C. uhibbu baytii
   D. fii l-matbakhi taawila

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
41. Translate into English: an-naafidhatu nadhiifa (2 marks)

42. Give three differences between the Arabic and the English alphabets. (3 marks) (3 marks)

43. Explain why it is important to know the days of the week. (2 marks) (2 marks)

44. Translate into English: al-misbaahu fawqa t-taawila (2 marks)

45. Describe how to carry out a dictation of the days of the week in pairs. (3 marks) (3 marks)

46. Translate into English: al-qittatu taHta s-sariir (2 marks)

47. Write five weather or environment words in Arabic (English letters are fine) with their meanings. (5 marks) (5 marks)

48. Explain what pace is and describe a good pace for reading aloud. (3 marks) (3 marks)

49. Give three tips that help a speaker to use tone and pace well. (3 marks) (3 marks)

50. Translate into English: ashrabu l-maa'a (2 marks)

51. Give three items from a peer review checklist for reading aloud. (3 marks) (3 marks)

52. Name three things that make Arabic writing different from English writing. (3 marks) (3 marks)

53. Give two polite words for interrupting or inviting someone to speak, with meanings. (2 marks) (2 marks)

54. Explain why dots are important in Arabic letters. Give an example. (3 marks) (3 marks)

55. Give three questions you could ask when you give peer feedback on a friend's fluency. (3 marks) (3 marks)

56. Name two common foods in your area and write one Arabic sentence about one of them, with its meaning. (3 marks) (3 marks)

57. Translate into English: al-jawwu baarid (2 marks)

58. Translate into English: uhibbu l-ʿasiira (2 marks)

59. Name four key words about the home in Arabic sounds with meanings. (4 marks) (4 marks)

60. Write one Arabic sentence about today's weather in sounds and translate it. (2 marks) (2 marks)

61. A four-line poem says: ʿaynii taraa, udhunii tasmaʿu, anfii yashummu, famii yatakallamu. Give the meaning of the first line and say what the poem is about. (3 marks) (3 marks)

62. Give three ways in which a family can reduce food wastage at home. (3 marks) (3 marks)
pages.answers:
ARABIC LANGUAGE — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #6 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. D — anaa tilmiidha
   A girl uses tilmiidha, with the ending -a. A boy says tilmiidh.

2. C — peace be upon you
   السَّلَامُ عَلَيْكُمْ (as-salaamu ʿalaykum) means peace be upon you.

3. D — I have a brother and a sister.
   عِنْدِي أَخٌ وَأُخْتٌ (ʿindii akh wa ukht) means: I have a brother and a sister.

4. C — الْمِصْبَاحُ فَوْقَ الطَّاوِلَةِ
   الْمِصْبَاحُ فَوْقَ الطَّاوِلَةِ (al-misbaahu fawqa t-taawila) means: The lamp is above the table.

5. C — The cat is under the bed.
   الْقِطَّةُ تَحْتَ السَّرِيرِ (al-qittatu taHta s-sariir) means: The cat is under the bed.

6. A — listen
   اِسْمَعْ (ismaʿ) means listen.

7. D — dawrii
   دَوْرِي is read dawrii and means my turn.

8. A — It makes a yes or no question
   hal begins a question that can be answered with naʿam or laa.

9. B — dawruka
   dawruka means 'your turn'. dawrii means 'my turn'.

10. D — oranges
   بُرْتُقَالٌ (burtuqaal) means oranges.

11. A — They act only on the correct instruction
   The game trains careful listening to instructions.

12. D — bi
   bi means 'with', so bi-yadii is 'with my hand'.

13. B — body
   جِسْمٌ (jism) means body.

14. C — sun
   شَمْسٌ (shams) means sun.

15. C — Plant trees and keep the surroundings clean
   Planting trees and keeping the area clean protect the environment.

16. C — How your voice sounds, for example friendly and clear
   Tone is the sound quality of your voice, such as calm, friendly and clear.

17. A — ma
   مَ is read ma.

18. B — la
   لَ is read la.

19. B — Daad
   The letter ض is called Daad.

20. C — Hello, Ahmad.
   مَرْحَبًا يَا أَحْمَدُ (marhaban yaa Ahmad) means: Hello, Ahmad.

21. C — jadda
   جَدَّةٌ is read jadda and means grandmother.

22. C — abun
   The syllables are read in order: a then bun gives abun (father).

23. B — anf
   أَنْفٌ is read anf and means nose.

24. B — batn
   بَطْنٌ is read batn and means stomach.

25. D — نَهْرٌ
   نَهْرٌ (nahr) means river.

26. D — نَافِذَةٌ
   نَافِذَةٌ (naafidha) means window.

27. B — milʿaqa
   مِلْعَقَةٌ is read milʿaqa and means spoon.

28. A — It shows where a letter joins to another
   The line is called a tatweel and shows joining.

29. B — ف (faa)
   The word fam (فَمٌ) starts with faa, which has one dot above.

30. A — From right to left
   Arabic is written from right to left.

31. B — سَاعَةٌ
   سَاعَةٌ (saaʿa) means clock.

32. B — jadiid
   جَدِيدٌ is read jadiid and means new.

33. A — الخميس
   Thursday begins with khaa (خ), which has one dot above.

34. B — al-ʿasiira
   We drink juice, not cake, a party or a balloon.

35. A — The spelling, dots and marks
   Checking the words helps to avoid mistakes.

36. B — Writing each letter in its correct shape
   Each letter must have its known shape so the reader can read it.

37. A — رَقَبَةٌ
   رَقَبَةٌ (raqaba) means neck.

38. B — الرِّيحُ قَوِيَّةٌ
   الرِّيحُ قَوِيَّةٌ (ar-riihu qawiyya) means: The wind is strong.

39. C — زَهْرَةٌ
   زَهْرَةٌ (zahra) means flower.

40. B — haadhaa baytii
   haadhaa baytii (This is my house) introduces the topic.

SECTION B
----
41. (2 marks)
   Answer: The window is clean.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

42. (3 marks)
   Answer: Arabic is read from right to left; it has no capital letters; letters join and change shape; it uses marks for short vowels; it has sounds like ʿayn and Haa that English does not have.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each valid difference, up to 3.

43. (2 marks)
   Answer: Days help us to plan what to do and to use time well, for example school, homework and rest.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for planning and 1 mark for good use of time.

44. (2 marks)
   Answer: The lamp is above the table.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

45. (3 marks)
   Answer: One learner says a day; the other repeats it, says the sounds and writes the letters from right to left; they check and correct together.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for saying the day, 1 mark for writing and 1 mark for checking.

46. (2 marks)
   Answer: The cat is under the bed.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

47. (5 marks)
   Answer: For example shams (sun), sahaab (clouds), matar (rain), riih (wind), samaa' (sky).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct word with its meaning.

48. (3 marks)
   Answer: Pace is the speed of reading. A good pace is steady, not too fast so that listeners understand, and not so slow that the sentence sounds broken.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the meaning and 2 marks for the description.

49. (3 marks)
   Answer: Speak loudly enough and clearly; speak at a steady speed; pause between sentences; smile when greeting.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each valid tip.

50. (2 marks)
   Answer: I drink water.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

51. (3 marks)
   Answer: Every word read correctly; steady pace; voice rises for questions; pauses at commas; voice shows feeling.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each valid item.

52. (3 marks)
   Answer: It is written from right to left; it has no capital letters; most letters join and change shape; short vowels are shown with marks.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each valid difference.

53. (2 marks)
   Answer: ʿafwan (excuse me) and tafaddal (please, go ahead).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each word with meaning.

54. (3 marks)
   Answer: Some letters have the same body shape and differ only by their dots. For example baa has one dot below, taa has two dots above and thaa has three dots above.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for same shape, 1 mark for dots make the difference and 1 mark for a correct example.

55. (3 marks)
   Answer: Were the words clear? Was the speed steady? Did the voice fall for statements and rise for questions?
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each suitable question.

56. (3 marks)
   Answer: For example maize and bananas. al-mawzu ladhiidh. The banana is delicious.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for two foods, 1 mark for a correct sentence and 1 mark for its meaning.

57. (2 marks)
   Answer: The weather is cold.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

58. (2 marks)
   Answer: I like juice.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

59. (4 marks)
   Answer: For example bayt (house), ghurfa (room), matbakh (kitchen), taawila (table).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct word with meaning.

60. (2 marks)
   Answer: For example al-jawwu baarid. The weather is cold.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for a correct sentence and 1 mark for the translation.

61. (3 marks)
   Answer: My eye sees. The poem says what a part of the body does: the eye sees, the ear hears, the nose smells and the mouth speaks.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the meaning of the line and 2 marks for the poem's idea.

62. (3 marks)
   Answer: Cook only what is needed; store leftovers and eat them later; share extra food; use peels for compost.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each sensible way.
